generalfeedback.text:
{@L2@} is parallel to {@par@}, which meets {@L1@} at {@cc@}. So the angle between {@L1@} and {@L2@} is angle {@nm@}.

The face {@face@} is isosceles ({@L1@} = V{@ee@} = {@se@} cm), so the perpendicular from V meets {@par@} at its midpoint. Then \(\cos {@nm@} = \frac{{@half@}}{{@se@}}\), so angle {@nm@} = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angle between skew lines in a pyramid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Find the angle between a sloping edge of a rectangular-based right pyramid and a base edge it does not meet.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 13, Section 2.5 and Figure 8(b) (the angle between skew lines of a pyramid) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: rectangular bases, new pairs, numbers and wording, randomised, with a naming step and named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: kA: is(charat(ans1,2) = "V"); kD: is(not kA and charat(ans1,3) = opp(cc));

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="kA"]]

Angle {@ans1@} is at V, between two sloping edges, and neither of them is parallel to {@L2@}. Slide {@L2@}, without turning it, until it meets {@L1@}: at which point do they meet?

[[else]][[if test="kD"]]

Angle {@ans1@} uses the diagonal of the base, which is not parallel to {@L2@}. Which line through {@cc@} is parallel to {@L2@}?

[[else]]

Angle {@ans1@} is between {@L1@} and {@oedge@}. In the rectangle ABCD, {@oedge@} is at right angles to {@L2@}, not parallel to it. Which line through {@cc@} is parallel to {@L2@}?

[[/if]][[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 90); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); adjv: if okr then float(se*cos(rdn)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: You used the base edge {@oedge@}, which is {@other@} cm long. In the rectangle ABCD, {@oedge@} is at right angles to {@L2@}. Use the base edge through {@cc@} that is parallel to {@L2@}.

You used the whole base edge, {@side@} cm, as the side next to the angle. The face {@face@} is isosceles, so the perpendicular from V meets that edge at its midpoint: what length is next to the angle?
That is the angle at V, between {@L1@} and the perpendicular from V to the base edge. You want the other acute angle of the same right-angled triangle, at {@cc@}.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

{@L1@} is {@se@} cm long, so with your angle the perpendicular from V would meet the base edge {@d2(adjv)@} cm from {@cc@}. Each sloping face is isosceles, so that foot must be the midpoint of a base edge. Which base edge through {@cc@} is parallel to {@L2@}, and what is half of it?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
